topic: Requirements to executable specifications and code generation

parts.title: Deconstructing Requirements into Public Method Contracts
parts.reason: NotebookLM sources cover only 20% of key terms (missing precondition, postcondition), making live slides best for teaching formal contract specifications.

parts.title: Structuring Executable Specifications in Spec-Driven Frameworks
parts.reason: NotebookLM sources cover 60% of key terms, so an explainer video works well to introduce BDD framework syntax despite missing Gherkin details.

parts.title: Step-by-Step Translation of Requirements to Executable Specs
parts.reason: Sources cover just 25% of terms (lacking assertion harnesses), so presenting the payment-processing worked example live on slides ensures complete technical clarity.

parts.title: Prompt Patterns for Generating Executable Specifications
parts.reason: NotebookLM sources cover only 20% of terms (lacking schema anchoring), so live slides are required to properly explain prompt architectures for spec generation.

parts.title: Hands-on Authoring of Executable Specs from Requirements
parts.reason: An in-class pair activity lets students practice authoring BDD executable specs for a session manager with immediate peer feedback.
